_meta.purpose: Step-1 join artifact. Curation seed for the boss generator. Curated by accolade/recognizability, NOT by FP rank.
_meta.scope: v1 = champions + iconic non-champions. Tier B deferred (flag).
_meta.join: Join to the computed 30x29 table on (season_code, team_code). team_code uses common abbreviations — CC must map to the repo's players.json `team` convention (one-time 30-team lookup).

axes.tier: champ | iconic  — recognizability/accolade axis. This is the eligibility gate.
axes.route: NOT stored. Computed by Step 1 from FP: below band -> handicap, above band -> raid, else daily.
axes.defensive_low: Hint only. Known low-FP defensive identity expected to route to HANDICAP. Curated IN, never dropped.
axes.name_team_level: Display names the team-season, not a literal five (used where nominal starters != the iconic lineup, e.g. '17 Warriors).

_meta.era_id: Scheduling-weight unit. No identity-era recurs within cooldown days. Multi-season identities share one era_id so e.g. the three Shaq-Kobe titles don't headline in the same week.

bosses.story: Jordan came back and the league exhaled too soon. 69 wins, Pippen and Rodman flanking the greatest closer alive. The dynasty didn't rebuild — it just resumed.
One more ring before they tore it all down. Jordan, Pippen, Rodman, running on fumes and spite. Everybody knew it was ending; nobody could make it end faster.
Robinson handed the keys to a second-year Duncan and the lockout season belonged to San Antonio. Two seven-footers, zero wasted motion. The blueprint starts here.
The most unstoppable force of his era, and a 21-year-old who already thought he was better. Shaq dunked, Kobe schemed, Phil watched it work. Ring one of three.
They stopped pretending anyone could guard them. Shaq was a cheat code, Kobe was the heir who wouldn't wait. 15-1 through the playoffs. Just unfair.
Three straight, the dynasty fully formed. By now the rest of the West played for second. Shaq in the post, Kobe everywhere else, the trophy a formality.
Robinson's farewell, Duncan's coronation. The Admiral walked off with a ring and the franchise in steady hands. Fundamentals don't go out of style.

bosses.flavor: five starters, no superstars, one ring
bosses.story: No superstars, no excuses — just five men who'd rather guard you than breathe. Billups iced it, Hamilton never stopped running, Prince and the Wallaces made the paint a no-fly zone. They out-toughed a Hall of Fame Lakers team. Detroit, baby.
Duncan, Parker, Ginobili — three generations of cold-blooded in one locker room. Manu off the bench like a problem nobody solved. Methodical, bilingual, lethal.
Shaq brought the gravity, Flash brought the dagger. Down 0-2, Wade simply decided the Finals were his. One of the great individual takeovers, ring attached.
No drama, no mercy. The Spurs ran the table on Cleveland like a machine clocking out on time. Duncan, Parker Finals MVP, and a defense that never blinked.
Garnett screamed it into existence — anything is possible. KG, Pierce, Ray Allen, a year together and a banner to show for it. Ubuntu, and the Lakers in six.
Kobe's first without Shaq, the one that proved it was always him. Gasol gave him a partner, Phil gave him the triangle, and the doubters gave it up.
Back-to-back, and the sweetest one came over Boston. Kobe willed Game 7 home on a miserable shooting night because losing to the Celtics wasn't an option.
The fadeaway that wouldn't miss and the team nobody picked. Dirk torched the superteam Heat, Chandler anchored the back, and a whole career got its ring.
They took their talents to South Beach and finally cashed the check. LeBron, Wade, Bosh — the villains of the league, validated. The promise, delivered.
66 wins, 27 straight, peak LeBron. The Ray Allen corner three saved the dynasty and broke San Antonio's heart. The best version of the Big Three era.
Revenge served in tic-tac-toe passing. The Spurs moved the ball until the Heat dizzied, then put it away. Kawhi arrived, Duncan ascended, basketball as art.
Curry and Thompson rained it down and changed the geometry of the game. The first crown of the new dynasty — light, fast, and three-pointers for days.
Down 3-1 to the 73-win Warriors, LeBron dragged Cleveland back from the dead. The block, the three, the promise kept. A city's 52-year wait, over.

bosses.flavor: Durant joins 73 wins — the Death Lineup era
bosses.story: Durant joined a 73-win team and the league filed a complaint. The Death Lineup with a second MVP — five shooters, no answer. Basketball on easy mode.
Back-to-back, and they swept the Cavs to do it. Durant, Curry, Iguodala off the bench — every closeout a foregone conclusion. The dynasty at full cruelty.
Kawhi's one perfect season, the load managed straight to a title. The Game 7 buzzer-beater that bounced four times, then a whole country celebrated. North.
LeBron and AD in the Orlando vacuum, ring for Kobe. No crowd, no road games, no doubt — the Lakers were the best team in the strangest season ever played.
The Greek Freak refused to leave and then refused to lose. 50 in the closeout, the block on Ayton, a small-market title carried on two enormous shoulders.
Everyone wrote them off after the injuries. Curry answered with Finals MVP at last and a fourth ring. The splash, the dynasty, back from the ashes.

bosses.flavor: the big man who sees everything
bosses.story: The big man who sees the whole floor before you do. Jokic triple-doubled Denver to its first title, Murray beside him, the league still underrating him somehow.
The most complete team in years, and they knew it all season. Tatum and Brown finished what Boston started, raising the franchise's record-breaking 18th.
The MVP turned a young Thunder team into a finished one. Gilgeous-Alexander's midrange clinic, a deep roster, and Oklahoma City's first ring. The future, now.
The best regular season anyone's ever played — and the one that got away. Curry's unanimous MVP, a record that may never fall, and a 3-1 lead they'll never forget.

bosses.flavor: Shaq, Kobe, Malone, Payton — and no ring
bosses.story: Shaq, Kobe, Malone, and Payton chasing one ring together. Two all-time greats joined for a coronation and got Detroit instead. The cautionary tale of stars.
Nash conducting offense as performance art, seven seconds and a problem for you. The most fun team that never won — fouled, suspended, and robbed of its shot.

bosses.flavor: the passing that should've won a title
bosses.story: The passing that should've won a title. Webber, Bibby, Divac, Stojakovic moving the ball like a rumor. Game 6 still keeps Sacramento up at night.

bosses.flavor: the MVP who stepped over them
bosses.story: 165 pounds of refusal. The MVP carried a role-player roster to the Finals and stepped over Tyronn Lue to remind everyone whose stage it was. The Answer.
Durant, Westbrook, Harden — three future MVPs, too young and too soon. They reached the Finals and got schooled, then got broken up before they could grow.
MVP, 66 wins, a city's whole hope on one set of shoulders. The first great Cleveland team, one Orlando series short. The ring would have to wait, and travel.

bosses.flavor: 65 wins, one Game 7 from the Warriors
bosses.story: 65 wins and a Game 7 from dethroning the Warriors — then the threes stopped falling, 27 straight misses. Harden's MVP year, an inch from history.

bosses.flavor: the floor was lava in Memphis
bosses.story: The floor was lava in Memphis. Gasol, Randolph, Conley, Tony Allen — they'd muck up your beautiful offense and dare you to play their way. Defense as identity.

bosses.flavor: throw it anywhere near the rim
bosses.story: Throw it anywhere near the rim and Blake or DeAndre would finish the sentence. Chris Paul running the show, the most electric team that never broke through.

bosses.flavor: Durant, Kyrie, Harden — for sixteen games
bosses.story: Durant, Kyrie, Harden — for sixteen healthy games, the scariest team alive. Then the injuries, the centimeter, the what-if. Basketball's great unfinished draft.
Trust the Process, then watch it almost work. Embiid bullying the paint, Simmons everywhere but the three-point line. Kawhi's bounce ended it. So close.
No center, switch everything, live and die by the three. Harden and Westbrook reinventing the position out of existence. The boldest gamble that didn't cash.
Two of the purest scorers alive, a mile high and a problem for any defense. Iverson and Anthony putting up points in bunches — fireworks short of a title.

bosses.flavor: Hakeem, Drexler, and Barkley chase one more
bosses.story: Hakeem, Drexler, and Barkley chasing one more before the legs gave out. Three Hall of Famers, all past their peak, all still terrifying. One last run.

bosses.flavor: a win from the Finals on the 73-win Warriors
bosses.story: A win from the Finals on the 73-win Warriors, then it slipped away. Durant and Westbrook had history in their hands. By summer, the partnership was over.

bosses.flavor: Dwight and the shooters reach the Finals
bosses.story: Dwight Howard at his most unstoppable, ringed by shooters who never missed. They shocked LeBron's Cavs and reached the Finals. Kobe's Lakers ended the cape.
Vince Carter took flight and the whole league stopped to watch. The most electric leaper of all time, dragging Toronto onto the map one poster at a time.
The 8-seed that ate the 67-win Mavs alive. Baron Davis, Stephen Jackson, a full-tilt underdog that scared the league straight. Believe, and they did.
